newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FALLING DOLLAR, RATES BOOST AUSTRALIAN FARMS-GOVT.
newsitem.headline: FALLING DOLLAR, RATES BOOST AUSTRALIAN FARMS-GOVT.

text.p: Falling interest rates and a lower Australian dollar would dramatically boost farm incomes, acting Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Thursday.
Fischer told reporters broadacre farm net incomes would jump more tha A$6,100 as a result.
The Reserve Bank has made five 50 basis point reductions to official cash rates since July 1996, the most recent on July 30 bringing official rates fown to 5.0 percent.
Average farm income in the fiscal year to June 30, 1997 fell to A$47,100 from A$50,520 in 1995/96, official figures released in June show.
